props.text: The case for the platform rebuild.

**TL;DR.** Our current platform is throttling delivery: every team hits the same handoff and review bottlenecks, and the cost of maintaining the legacy stack is now ~30% of engineering time. A six-month rebuild on a shared design system + token-driven workflow brings iteration speed back, reduces ongoing maintenance, and unblocks the H2 product roadmap. We recommend green-lighting by end of month.

items: **Handoff drag.** Designers spend 40% of cycle time on dev handoff because tokens live in Figma but not in code — every spec gets re-translated.
**Review focused on pixels, not intent.** Engineers can't tell whether a 2px gap is intentional or a bug, so reviews stall on minutiae.
**Maintenance debt compounds.** Three competing CSS systems (legacy SCSS, in-house tokens v1, new tokens v2) mean every component change touches three files.
**Unified token system in code** (Q3). Single source of truth, generated from Figma, consumed by both web and mobile.
**Component library migration** (Q3-Q4). Move 40 production components to the new system; archive legacy SCSS.
**Review-as-intent workflow** (Q4). Reviews focus on layout intent and accessibility, not pixel diffs.
**Budget:** $480k for tools, infrastructure, and contractor time across H2.
**Decision:** green-light by end of month so we can staff Q3 cleanly.

props.text: Pilot teams using the rebuilt workflow have shipped production work **3.2× faster** (internal study, n=24 teams). Applied to our roadmap, that pulls H2 shipping milestones in by ~6 weeks and frees ~15% of engineering capacity for new product work in 2027.
